ThreatFox classifies this exact SHA-256 as a high-confidence SantaStealer payload. Ward independently hashed identical Fluxus V7.exe files in two public Roblox-executor repositories and found an embedded PowerShell loader with Defender exclusion, hidden download, elevation, execution, and scheduled-task persistence behavior.

Ward independently hashed Built.exe at the pinned repository commit. VirusTotal labels the exact sample trojan.python/bdoj and categorizes it as trojan, spyware, and dropper. Static PyInstaller inspection also found an encrypted blank.aes payload bundled with rar.exe and rarreg.key.

MediaFire's public API reports this exact SHA-256 for the live 44,809,454-byte Installer.rar in folder xpuwhpaw2jpbi. Ward independently downloaded and hash-verified the archive, extracted it only inside Kali with the README-published password, and found one unsigned Windows loader.

Ward independently hashed Installer/Installer.exe from the password-protected archive. Static PE and control-flow analysis found retained chacha20_xor, gpo_exclude, want_uac, and gpo_open symbols and confirmed appended-payload decryption, Windows Defender policy exclusions, LOCALAPPDATA staging, and elevated launch behavior. The file was not executed.

Ward fetched and hashed the live public Setup.ps1 stage inside Kali. Bounded static decoding verified ten authenticated AES layers and recovered a fetch-and-execute command for the next encrypted PowerShell stage. The script was not executed.

Ward fetched and hashed the live update.ps1 wrapper inside Kali and decoded it statically. The recovered script geofences CIS country codes, adds a Defender exclusion, captures and uploads a screenshot with system metadata, downloads an encrypted archive, and launches its extracted PE. The script was not executed.

Ward independently hashed the live password-protected archive inside Kali. Static inspection with the password embedded in the decoded loader found one Windows PE at 1/1.exe. The archive contents were not executed.

Ward independently hashed the 1/1.exe payload extracted only inside Kali from the live encrypted archive. The enclosing decoded loader explicitly starts this PE after screenshot exfiltration and Defender exclusion changes. The packed PE was statically inspected and not executed.

Ward independently downloaded and hashed the live password-protected GitHub release archive inside Kali on 2026-11-02. The archive was extracted with the password published in the pinned README and was not executed.

Ward independently hashed libcurl.dll from the live release. Static PE analysis confirmed curl proxy exports, CreateThread and VirtualAlloc imports, and an initialization path that reconstructs code from the custom .39ca68 section. The DLL was not executed.

Derived SHA-256 of the 7,168-byte code blob reconstructed by Ward's bounded static decoder from libcurl.dll section .39ca68. This is a derived artifact for correlation, not a claim that the bytes were executed.

Ward independently fetched and hashed the live PowerShell wrapper inside Kali. Static extraction decoded its outer base64 layer and established that it downloads a PNG carrier, parses attacker-controlled tEXt chunks, reconstructs a PE and C# loader, and invokes the loader in memory. The script was not executed.

Ward independently fetched and hashed the live PNG carrier inside Kali. A bounded parser recovered metadata, 31 X chunks, one Y chunk, an XOR key, a PE payload, and embedded C# source without interpreting or executing the content.

Ward independently reconstructed and hashed main_2.exe from the live PNG carrier inside Kali. The enclosing decoded C# performs process hollowing or writes and starts the PE from a random temporary directory. Ward's transient file scanner recorded the exact bytes under scan fc08a533-a06d-4b1d-83e3-803a07eec806; the PE was not executed and no final family name is asserted.

indicators.campaign: gerhodd.com GitHub Pages Electron delivery wave
indicators.validation_notes: GitHub publishes this digest for the current 199,561,175-byte release asset. Ward independently downloaded and hash-verified the live archive only inside Kali on 2026-11-02. The archive tells victims to add the installer to Defender exclusions or disable real-time protection and was not executed.

indicators.campaign: gerhodd.com GitHub Pages Electron delivery wave
indicators.validation_notes: Ward independently hashed release-x64.exe from the current GitHub release. Bounded extraction identified an NSIS-wrapped Electron application whose main.js decrypts attacker-supplied JavaScript with a hard-coded AES-256-CBC key and executes the plaintext with new Function. The PE was not executed.

indicators.campaign: gerhodd.com GitHub Pages Electron delivery wave
indicators.validation_notes: Ward independently extracted and hashed resources/app.asar from the current Electron bundle. A bounded ASAR parser recovered main.js and verified its SHA-256 against the archive header without loading Electron or JavaScript.

indicators.campaign: gerhodd.com GitHub Pages Electron delivery wave
indicators.validation_notes: Ward independently extracted and hashed runtimec0cc.dat from the current Electron bundle. The recovered main.js reads this file, uses its first 16 bytes as an IV, decrypts the remainder with a hard-coded AES-256-CBC key, and passes the plaintext to new Function.

indicators.campaign: gerhodd.com GitHub Pages Electron delivery wave
indicators.validation_notes: Derived SHA-256 of the 604,800-byte JavaScript plaintext recovered by Ward's bounded AES-CBC decoder from runtimec0cc.dat. Static control-flow identifiers and the application-ready path establish Defender exclusion, elevation, encrypted-payload execution, environment checking, installation, and self-destruction routines. The script was not executed and its final embedded payload remains unresolved.

Ward independently hashed the password-protected Filmora ZIP collected from the public LibreHub route. It was extracted only inside ward-remnux:0.8.0 with network disabled and read-only sample mounts. No member was executed.

Ward independently hashed Installer.exe from the collected Filmora archive. Bounded static PE reconstruction and decompilation established ICMLuaUtil CoGetObject and ShellExec auto-elevation, self-relaunch with marker RQFTIRXS, and PEB process masquerading as explorer.exe. The PE was not executed.
